quick.summary: Why a broken table stayed broken for a week, and the one field that fixes it.
quick.takeaway: Every table names a team that answers for it.

beats.line: A table broke on Monday. By Friday nobody had fixed it. Why?
No idea. Whoever built it left last year.
Then nobody does. Unowned tables stay broken.
Record an owner on every table. A team, not one person.

board.text: owner: a team, with a contact

beats.line: Why a team? A person is clearer.
People leave and go on holiday. A team stays reachable.
And check owners when someone moves on.
Owner: the payments data team, with their channel.
Next Monday, the alert has somewhere to go.

quiz.question: Who should be recorded as the owner of a data table?
options: A team with a contact point
quiz.explanation: A team stays reachable when individuals leave or are away, so problems reach someone who can act.

quiz.question: A table with no recorded owner is more likely to stay broken.
quiz.explanation: With no owner, nobody is clearly responsible, so everyone assumes someone else will fix it.
